o.text: From Persian خاله (xâle), ultimately from Arabic خالة (ḵāla).

glosses: cowshed, sheep cote (a structure where animals are held)

o.text: From Old Anatolian Turkish طام (d̥am, dam), from Proto-Turkic *tām.
From müjdə (“good news”) + -çi. Doublet of muştuluqçu.
Morphologically from yapışmaq (“to stick, intransitive”) + -dır. Cognate with Chuvash ҫыпӑҫтар (śyp̬ăśtar), etc.
From ümum- + milli. Likely a calque of Russian общенациона́льный (obščenacionálʹnyj).
From Proto-Common Turkic *kaya, from Proto-Turkic *k(i)aya. See more at Turkish kaya.

Borrowed from Armenian մամուռ (mamuṙ).
The native Turkic word for moss, yosun, has shifted its meaning to signify 'seaweed' in Azerbaijani.
From yanılt- + -mac. Cognate with Kyrgyz жаңылтмач (jaŋıltmac).
